narr: On the morning of the 21st, a cold front extended southwestward from southern ON to far-northwestern OH. This front drifted southeastward through the early evening, when it became located in vicinity of the major axis of Lake Erie, west-central OH, and east-central IN. The front then moved little through the wee hours of the 22nd. A line of thunderstorms moved generally eastward across northwest PA during the early evening and generated isolated straight-line wind damage. The ambient environment consisted of moderate to strong effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively. Repeated thunderstorms training over the same areas of Erie and Crawford Counties in PA led to excessive rainfall and flash flooding. Total rainfall amounts of 3 to 5 inches were estimated by radar in these locations.
ev: Widespread flash flood in Union City. Several homes evacuated in the area of North Main and Waterford Streets and South Main and Parade Streets in Union City. Academy Drive near the junior high and high school was washed out due to flooding. Reports of several basements and homes flooded. Radar estimated rainfall of 3 to 5 inches in far southeast Erie county. US-6 bridge abutment washed away due to flooding near King Road northeast of Elgin.
lsr: ERIE COUNTY REPORTED EVACUATIONS ARE OCCURRING IN THE AREA OF NORTH MAIN AND WATERFORD STREETS AND SOUTH MAIN AND PARADE STREETS IN UNION CITY BOROUGH DUE TO FLOODING.
